components.gap: Definitions of formula-level IP/NIP and theory-level NIP are present (def:p03-nip), but no shattering/type-count characterization is stated or proved. The chosen characterization (for example: phi is NIP iff for some n no n-element set is shattered, iff the number of phi-types over finite sets is polynomially bounded), with all quantifiers explicit, and its proof are owed.

No reconstruction of the actual 1971 Stability, the f.c.p., and Superstability presentation appears; the paper is only cited in grouped citations. The other two same-year Shelah papers (the ultrapower paper and the unstable-spectrum paper Shelah1971NonIsomorphicModels) are not distinguished from it anywhere on the route.

Stable implies NIP, stable implies simple, and simple plus NIP implies stable are only stated (lines 375-380, 626-629, table rows) with grouped citations; no theory-level proof of any of the three implications is written.

The random graph is asserted simple, unstable and IP, and DLO/RCF are asserted o-minimal and NIP with DLO unstable, but no witnessing or nonwitnessing argument is written: no order-property witness for the random graph or DLO, no shattering witness for the edge relation, no proof that forking in the random graph has local character, no quantifier-elimination argument for o-minimality of DLO or RCF, and no argument that o-minimal theories are NIP. RCF's instability is not stated.

A four-row dividing-line table is present, but the separation of a single NIP formula in an arbitrary theory from Simon's later results that require an ambient NIP theory is not made anywhere, and the table's implication column is discharged by grouped citation only.

Simple theory is defined by local character of forking only. The tree-property/local-character equivalence is delegated to 'the cited sources establish the equivalence' (a citation in place of a proof), and no dividing/forking facts (e.g. Kim's lemma, forking equals dividing in simple theories, symmetry, transitivity) or the base bound |A| <= |T| + |x| are proved.

components.gap: Composite: GOAL-01 is supplied, but GOAL-02 (precise language and level hypotheses of the stated relationships) and GOAL-03 (actual ordered examples and boundary cases) are only partly supplied, so the composite survey is not complete.

The relationships (stable implies NIP, o-minimal implies NIP, o-minimal does not imply stable, simple plus NIP implies stable) are stated, but not all with their precise language hypotheses: DLO's language is never fixed; 'o-minimal implies NIP' is stated only at theory level with no statement of the structure-to-theory transfer (Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn) that makes 'o-minimal structure' and 'o-minimal theory' interchangeable; and the claim in def:p03-o-minimal that o-minimality is 'strictly stronger than merely being NIP' has no witnessing NIP non-o-minimal ordered example in a stated language.

Only DLO and RCF are named as ordered examples (without argument), and the only boundary case given is DLO's instability. No ordered boundary case shows that an expansion can lose o-minimality or NIP (e.g. an ordered structure with an infinite definable discrete set, or the ordered real field expanded by a predicate for the integers), and no NIP ordered structure that is not o-minimal is given. The text does not claim arbitrary expansions preserve NIP or o-minimality, so that failure condition does not hold, but the required boundary cases are absent.
